name: ADIA
coverage: Selected Abu Dhabi Investment Authority relationships in India, covering a listed bank and retailer, private businesses, a fund manager and housing funds. Older disclosures retain their own dates.
limitations: Selective public-disclosure coverage, not a complete portfolio or a live ownership register. The review date does not update the date of an older holding disclosure.
Ownership belongs to the named entity, fund, subsidiary or platform. Fund commitments, acquisitions of assets and joint-venture stakes are not holdings in the listed parent.
Announced investments remain proposed unless closing evidence was reviewed. An unavailable percentage is not zero.
Investment themes and business cases are research interpretations of the cited activity, not forecasts or recommendations.

companies.name: H-CARE affordable-housing funds
companies.relationship: ADIA describes completed commitments to H-CARE 1 and 2.
companies.ownership: Fund investor; ownership percentage not disclosed
companies.ownershipDate: 2016/2017 commitments; ADIA case study reviewed 23 Oct 2026
companies.summary: These are fund-level investments financing residential projects, distinct from equity in the fund manager.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: housing-finance partnerships address demand for affordable and mid-market homes.
companies.risks: Developer credit, project delays, liquidity and real-estate cycles.

companies.name: HDFC Capital Advisors
companies.relationship: A November 2022 HDFC filing identifies ADIA’s ownership in HCAL.
companies.ownership: 10% of HCAL equity in historical filing
companies.ownershipDate: 15 Nov 2022 disclosure; current percentage not refreshed
companies.summary: This stake is in the manager, not a 10% interest in every H-CARE fund or a stake in listed HDFC Bank.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: manager ownership provides a different economic exposure from fund commitments.
companies.risks: Manager economics, governance, dilution and source age.

companies.name: IDFC FIRST Bank
companies.relationship: The bank announced a proposed CCPS issue of approximately ₹2,624 crore to Platinum Invictus B 2025 RSC Limited, an ADIA subsidiary.
companies.ownership: CCPS investment proposed; current equity percentage unverified
companies.summary: The named ADIA vehicle is distinct from Warburg Pincus affiliate Currant Sea. No conversion or closing percentage is inferred.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: bank capital can support lending expansion if asset quality and funding remain sound.
companies.risks: Credit costs, approvals, conversion terms and dilution.

companies.name: IIFL Home Finance
companies.relationship: The company’s milestone page records ADIA acquiring 20% following a capital infusion.
companies.ownership: 20% at disclosed acquisition milestone; current stake not refreshed
companies.summary: This is exposure to IIFL Home Finance, not ownership of the listed parent company.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: affordable-housing credit can grow with formalisation and household demand.
companies.risks: Borrower credit, funding costs, regulation and historical-data limits.

companies.name: Lenskart Solutions
companies.relationship: Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, acting through Platinum Owl C 2018 RSC Limited, sold 35 million shares.
companies.ownership: 35,000,000 shares sold; retained percentage not verified
companies.summary: The sale is attributed to the named ADIA-affiliated trust. It is not classified as a full exit.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: retail reach and manufacturing scale can support consumer growth.
companies.risks: Valuation, execution, margins and uncertainty over the residual holding.

companies.name: Reliance Retail Ventures
companies.relationship: Reliance announced a ₹4,966.80 crore investment by an ADIA subsidiary in 2023.
companies.ownership: Investment disclosed; total current percentage not verified
companies.summary: The investment is in RRVL, not directly in listed Reliance Industries. Announced incremental equity is not treated as total retained ownership.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: an omni-channel retail platform offers exposure to formalising consumption.
companies.risks: Competition, capital allocation, valuation and private-market liquidity.

events.title: ADIA-affiliated trust sells Lenskart shares
events.detail: The deal announcement reports a sale of 35 million shares through exchange trading platforms.
events.qualification: A sale of this size establishes reduction, not a full exit; the remaining holding was not reconciled.

report.title: ADIA in India
report.summary: ADIA’s disclosed Indian activity spans public and private equity, infrastructure and property. The six selected records distinguish subsidiaries, trusts, manager ownership and fund commitments, with the Lenskart sale recorded as a reduction.

sections.title: Long-horizon approach
sections.text: ADIA describes a diversified, multi-asset strategy and established a GIFT City subsidiary for Indian investments. This is portfolio context, not evidence of any particular company percentage.

sections.title: Financial services and housing
sections.text: The bank CCPS proposal, IIFL acquisition milestone, HCAL equity and H-CARE commitments are four distinct exposures. Their percentages are not interchangeable.

sections.title: Consumer exposure and monetisation
sections.text: Reliance Retail’s announcement and the Lenskart trust’s sale provide dated evidence of investment and reduction. Neither establishes a complete current portfolio.

themes.name: Housing and financial services
themes.case: Research interpretation: the disclosed relationships point to recurring interest in financial intermediation and housing supply.
themes.watch: Credit quality, financing terms and legal investment level.

themes.name: Consumer platforms
themes.case: Research interpretation: retail investments provide exposure to consumer distribution, with exit execution influencing retained exposure.
themes.watch: Valuation, operating performance and residual holdings.
